summary: The diff is well-structured (matches the existing run()/json.loads()/fail() wrapper pattern in task-gateway.py, valid YAML, 17/17 tests pass, no .github/workflows touched) but does not actually deliver the round-2 fix it claims. I directly ran scripts/ddl_authorization_check.py against crafted prompt text and confirmed two real weaknesses: (1) GRANT/REVOKE, CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION ... SECURITY DEFINER, and ALTER ROLE ... SUPERUSER -- classic Postgres privilege-escalation primitives, arguably more dangerous than CREATE INDEX/CREATE SEQUENCE which the keyword list does cover -- all pass through as {"valid": true}, completely undetected; risk-tier.py's path-based merge-time gate would not catch these either since this is prompt-text authorizing a live MCP call, not a schema-file diff. (2) The commit message's 'real citation check' and the script's own docstring claim a PRE-APPROVED-LIVE-DDL reference 'is not something a worker can fabricate by just writing a plausible-looking word' -- I tested this directly with a fabricated, non-existent ID (PRE-APPROVED-LIVE-DDL: KE-20260726-999999-dead) alongside a DROP TABLE statement, and it passed validation. The check only validates that the reference matches a regex shape, never that it corresponds to a real decision-log entry or file -- so the documentation's central claim about this round's fix is factually wrong. Since this task exists specifically to close detection weaknesses found in a prior real AUDIT REJECT, shipping a round 2 that still has an undetected privilege-escalation class and a spoofable citation check (while asserting in the docstring that it isn't spoofable) creates false confidence rather than closing the gap. The runtime-interception limitation is honestly disclosed; these two gaps are not.
issues: DDL keyword list omits GRANT/REVOKE, CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION (incl. SECURITY DEFINER), CREATE/ALTER/DROP ROLE, CREATE/DROP VIEW, and similar DCL/privilege-escalation statements -- verified live that GRANT ALL ON ... TO anon, a SECURITY DEFINER function, and ALTER ROLE ... SUPERUSER all return {"valid": true}

The PRE-APPROVED-LIVE-DDL citation check validates format only (regex shape of a KE-<date>-<time>-<hex> ID or OWNER_DECISIONS_NEEDED_<date>.yaml filename), not existence -- a fabricated, non-existent ID passes; the docstring's claim that this 'is not something a worker can fabricate' is contradicted by direct testing and should either be fixed (cross-check the citation against a real decision-log/file) or the documentation corrected to disclose this as a known limitation, same as the runtime-interception gap already is
No .github/workflows/** files touched -- hard rule from SUPERBOSS_DISPATCH_PROMPT.md not implicated
